Subject: Multiparametric MRI Prostate | Date: 15 February 2025 | Facility: Radboudumc

Clinical Indication:
Re-assessment prompted by a rising prostate-specific antigen level of 16.5 ng/mL alongside a previously positive biopsy result. Detailed local staging is required to address current clinical suspicion.

FINDINGS:
Prostatic dimensions yield a total volume of 29.08 mL. T2-weighted sequences highlight a distinctly hypointense focus within the left mid-gland peripheral zone, measuring roughly 12 × 8 × 10 mm. Diffusion-weighted imaging confirms marked restriction with correspondingly low apparent diffusion coefficient values. Dynamic contrast evaluation shows early focal enhancement. There is no evidence of extraprostatic extension or seminal vesicle invasion. Pelvic lymph nodes appear normal, and bone marrow signal remains unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left mid-peripheral zone. Prostate volume 29.08 mL yields a PSA density of 0.567 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.8393857.
